findings.reason: kubeclient.go:106-110 pass client-go secret.Data (already decoded) to decodeSecretKey, which decodes again at :177-179 whenever isBase64 holds. The operator generates 16-character passwords from letters, digits and !@#$%^&* (utils/kubernetes.py:1428-1429), so about 14% are pure alphanumeric, length 16, and will decode to different bytes. Authentication then fails on the default cluster path.
findings.claim: Cluster credential resolution base64-decodes already-decoded secret values that happen to look like base64, corrupting valid credentials.
findings.evidence: ResolveFromCluster passes the already-decoded secret.Data values to decodeSecretKey, which decodes them again whenever isBase64 succeeds. For example, a legitimate username 'test' becomes bytes b5eb2d, and password 'YWJjZGVmZ2hpamts' becomes 'abcdefghijkl'. authenticate then sends these changed credentials.

members.claim: Cluster credential resolution corrupts valid credentials that happen to match base64 syntax, preventing authentication.

findings.reason: resolveURL returns Endpoints.Admin first (kubeclient.go:149). keycloak_reconciler.py:464-466 always sets admin/public to http://{name}-keycloak.{ns}.svc.cluster.local:8080. The documented cluster-mode examples in migration-toolkit.md and export-realms.md leave out --server-url, and nothing sets up port forwarding, so the documented flow fails from outside the cluster.
findings.claim: Without --server-url, cluster mode picks status.endpoints.admin, which is an in-cluster svc.cluster.local address, so the documented workstation command can't connect.
findings.evidence: Without --server-url, resolveURL returns status.endpoints.admin. src/keycloak_operator/services/keycloak_reconciler.py:464 sets both admin and public to http://{name}-keycloak.{namespace}.svc.cluster.local:8080. The importer connects directly to that address without establishing forwarding, while the documented cluster-mode examples omit --server-url.

findings.reason: importer.go:76 and :82 return nil instead of result after earlier batches have added to result.Added and result.Skipped. printImportSummary in cmd/import_users.go returns early on nil, so runImportUsers' 'print partial result' never prints the earlier progress.
findings.claim: HTTP or token-refresh failures in later batches return a nil result, so the partial summary of earlier committed batches is lost.
findings.evidence: After a successful first batch updates result.Added and result.Skipped, an HTTP failure in batch two returns nil instead of result; token-refresh failures do the same at line 76. runImportUsers attempts to print the partial summary, but printImportSummary immediately returns for nil.

members.claim: Failures in later batches discard the accumulated result, hiding the changes already committed by earlier batches.

findings.reason: authenticate and importBatch use http.DefaultClient.Do, which has no Timeout, and runImportUsers passes context.Background() (import_users.go:344) with no deadline. A server that accepts the connection but never answers blocks the command indefinitely.
findings.claim: There is no HTTP timeout or context deadline, so a stalled server hangs the import forever.
findings.evidence: Both authenticate and importBatch use http.DefaultClient.Do and unbounded io.ReadAll calls. runImportUsers supplies context.Background() without a timeout. A server that accepts a connection but never finishes its response therefore prevents the command from completing or reporting failure.

members.claim: A stalled HTTP server can leave the import waiting indefinitely because neither requests nor their context have a deadline.

findings.reason: The importResp struct only reads added, skipped and errors, and ImportResult and printImportSummary have no overwritten field. Keycloak's PartialImportResults reports replaced resources under 'overwritten', so a run with --mode overwrite that replaces users shows Added 0 and Skipped 0.
findings.claim: Overwrite counts from the Partial Import response are dropped, so overwrite mode reports zero changes.
findings.evidence: The response struct reads only added, skipped and errors, and ImportResult and printImportSummary likewise have no overwritten count. A response with added=0, skipped=0 and overwritten=500 therefore produces an all-zero outcome summary. Keycloak reports replacements through getOverwritten() in [PartialImportResults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/keycloak/keycloak/26.4.0/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/partialimport/PartialImportResults.java).

members.claim: Successful overwrites are omitted from the import result, so overwrite mode can change every user while reporting zero changes.

findings.reason: importer_test.go contains only TestChunk_* and loader_test.go only TestLoadUsersFile_*. No test calls ImportUsers, authenticate, importBatch, ResolveFromCluster or decodeSecretKey, which is why the X1 decode bug got through. This is a test-coverage gap, so it stays low.
